principles: Preserve the existing Parallel Wave L0/non-authoritative boundary.
Document only the integration contract that future runtime code can later implement mechanically.
Keep proof and claim unlock sequential even when implementation planning is parallel.
drivers: User approved adding the integration model directly into the capability document.
Current runtime has read-only Parallel Wave projections but no full Parallel Development executor.
Capability wording must avoid overclaiming authority or proof from planning artifacts.

options.name: A: Compose Parallel Development on top of frozen Parallel Wave snapshots
pros: Reuses existing planning commands without changing their authority boundary.
Creates a clear future implementation path for workstream state and merge queue enforcement.
cons: Requires future commands to materialize execution state; the document must be explicit that this is not runnable yet.

options.name: B: Merge Parallel Wave and Parallel Development into one capability
cons: Risks implying read-only Wave output can execute, prove, or authorize claims, which conflicts with current command policy.

chosen: A: Compose Parallel Development on top of frozen Parallel Wave snapshots
rationale: Option A keeps the existing safe planning surface intact while giving Parallel Development a concrete input contract for future execution coordination.

preMortem.scenario: Reader treats wave output as authority evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Integration wording says Wave drives proof or unlocks claims.
preMortem.consequence: Parallel planning projection could be misused as PASS evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: State repeatedly that Wave is lineage/planning only and claims consume real gate evidence.
